function.mechanism: Acetyl substitution changes starch hydration and rheology, reducing retrogradation and improving processing stability in formulated foods.

adi.basis: EFSA re-evaluation of modified starches (including E1420) concluded there is no need for a numerical ADI (ADI not specified context).

efsa.key_finding: EFSA concluded no safety concern for modified starches, including E1420, at reported uses and use levels in the general population.

adi.basis: WHO/JECFA database lists ADI as NOT SPECIFIED for modified starches (including starch acetate).

concerns.summary: An 89-week mouse study including starch acetate at very high dietary levels reported some urinary/renal findings and GI enlargement, but no carcinogenicity signal for tested products.
Recent PubMed literature on acetylated starch is mostly functionality/technology focused, with limited new long-term human safety epidemiology specific to E1420.
key_references: PubMed query: acetylated starch food additive safety

concerns.summary: EFSA reports modified starches are hydrolyzed and fermented in the intestine; this indicates GI processing effects but did not translate into a regulatory safety concern at reported uses.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2017: no safety concern at reported uses; no need for a numerical ADI.
JECFA: ADI NOT SPECIFIED for modified starches including starch acetate.
No IARC monograph classification found for starch acetate/acetylated starch in the searched IARC resources.

populations: toddlers/high consumers (group-level modified starch exposure highest in EFSA scenarios)
adi_exceedance.notes: E1420-specific numeric ADI exceedance cannot be calculated because EFSA/JECFA use a non-numerical ADI framework (ADI not specified).

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory evaluations are consistently permissive with ADI-not-specified conclusions and no major carcinogenic classification, while residual uncertainty mainly comes from limited E1420-specific modern long-term human data.
key_factors: EFSA 2017 no-safety-concern conclusion for modified starches including E1420
JECFA ADI NOT SPECIFIED with latest listed evaluation year 2021 (specification update)
U.S. CFR listing at 21 CFR 172.892 with explicit treatment/residual limits
FDA food substance entry indicates Direct Food Substances Affirmed as GRAS for food starch-modified
